newsitem.title: CANADA: Protest stops Interfor logging on island.
newsitem.headline: Protest stops Interfor logging on island.

text.p: The environmental group Greenpeace said on Friday that 70 activists and native Indians today halted logging by International Forest Products Ltd on King Island in British Columbia.

"Approximately 70 people blockaded the main access road, so no logging is going on," said Greenpeace spokeswoman Tzeporah Berman. The island is near the town of Bella Coola on the central Pacific coast.

A company spokeswoman said she did not have the latest information from the site but believed logging was halted. She said the company already had an injunction barring protestors from the area and would attempt to enforce it.

Greenpeace said the forested valleys in the area were sacred to the Nuxalk people and environmentally sensitive. The Great Bear forest on the island was "the largest contiguous unprotected rain forest in British Columbia and is a forest of global ecological signifiance," Greenpeace said.
The local natives previously asked Interfor to stop logging the area.
